Quince.blurb: A direct-to-consumer brand that sells factory-direct basics — Mongolian cashmere, European linen, organic cotton and silk — at lower prices by cutting out wholesale markups.
Quince.catalog_note: Not everything Quince sells is 100% natural; many pieces contain elastane or blends. The items below are the ones that are.

Organic Basics.blurb: A Copenhagen brand built around GOTS-certified organic cotton underwear, tees and everyday basics, with a stated focus on lower-impact factories.
Organic Basics.catalog_note: Some of its activewear uses recycled synthetics. Only the all-natural pieces are listed here.

Colored Organics.blurb: A family-run children's brand making GOTS-certified organic cotton baby and kids' clothing, from bodysuits and pajamas to dresses and sweaters.
Colored Organics.catalog_note: Nearly the whole range is 100% organic cotton.

Little Sleepies.blurb: A children's and family sleepwear brand known for soft pajamas, zippies and matching family sets.
Little Sleepies.catalog_note: Only the pieces whose composition meets the 100%-natural rule are listed here.

Gap.blurb: The American mall staple since 1969 — denim, tees, khakis and sweats for the whole family.
Gap.catalog_note: Most of Gap's range contains synthetics. This page is the all-natural part of it.

Old Navy.blurb: Gap Inc.'s value brand, launched in 1994, selling family basics at low prices.
Old Navy.catalog_note: Most of Old Navy contains synthetics. These are the all-natural pieces.

Everlane.blurb: A San Francisco brand founded in 2010 that publishes its factories and cost breakdowns; known for organic cotton tees, linen, cashmere and denim.
Everlane.catalog_note: Everlane also sells stretch and blended pieces; only the all-natural ones appear here.

Pact.blurb: A Boulder, Colorado brand making GOTS-certified organic cotton basics — underwear, tees, loungewear and bedding — in Fair Trade Certified factories.
Pact.catalog_note: Pact's organic cotton basics; pieces that add elastane are left out.

Jungmaven.blurb: A hemp clothing brand making tees, sweats and basics in hemp and hemp/organic-cotton blends, sewn in the USA.
Jungmaven.catalog_note: Much of the range is a hemp and organic cotton blend — both natural fibers — so it qualifies, and the composition is shown on each item.

Smartwool.blurb: A merino wool brand founded in 1994 in Steamboat Springs, Colorado, best known for socks and base layers.
Smartwool.catalog_note: Many Smartwool pieces blend merino with nylon for durability. Only the all-wool items are listed here.

Faherty.blurb: A family-founded brand with a surf-and-beach sensibility, known for sun-washed tees, flannels and knit sweaters.
Faherty.catalog_note: Faherty's performance and 'Movement' lines are synthetic blends; only the all-natural pieces are listed here.

Taylor Stitch.blurb: A San Francisco menswear brand making workwear-inspired shirts, chinos and knits in organic cotton, hemp and wool, much of it released through small pre-order runs.
Taylor Stitch.catalog_note: A few chinos and tees add elastane; those are left out.

Frank & Eileen.blurb: A Los Angeles brand built around the button-up shirt, cut from Italian-woven cottons and linens, with a growing line of terry and knit basics.
Frank & Eileen.catalog_note: Nearly everything is 100% cotton or linen.

FLAX.blurb: A women's linen label making relaxed, roomy dresses, pants and tunics in a wide size range.
FLAX.catalog_note: Almost the entire line is 100% linen.

Magic Linen.blurb: A Lithuanian brand sewing clothing and home textiles from European linen, sold in dozens of colourways.
Magic Linen.catalog_note: Clothing is linen throughout; a few pieces blend linen with cotton.

NAADAM.blurb: A New York cashmere brand that buys fibre directly from herders in Mongolia and is known for its lower-priced basics.
NAADAM.catalog_note: Some pieces blend cashmere with wool or cotton — both natural — and the composition is shown on each item.

Icebreaker.blurb: A New Zealand merino wool brand making base layers, socks and outdoor clothing.
Icebreaker.catalog_note: Many Icebreaker pieces blend merino with nylon or Tencel; only the all-natural items appear here.

Toad&Co.blurb: A Santa Barbara brand making casual clothing in hemp, organic cotton and wool, with a long-standing focus on lower-impact fabrics.
Toad&Co.catalog_note: Toad&Co also uses Tencel and recycled synthetics; those pieces are left out.

Boden.blurb: A British family-clothing brand known for bright prints and classic cuts, with its Mini Boden line for children.
Boden.catalog_note: Much of the range is 100% cotton; pieces with elastane or viscose are left out.

Hill House.blurb: A New York brand best known for the Nap Dress, making dresses and separates in cotton poplin, linen and knits.
Hill House.catalog_note: Only the single-fiber pieces are listed; a few styles use blends.

Alicia Adams Alpaca.blurb: A New York label making wraps, sweaters and throws from baby alpaca.

All Cotton and Linen.blurb: A small brand selling cotton and linen clothing and home textiles, named for exactly what it sells.
All Cotton and Linen.catalog_note: The range is 100% cotton or 100% linen throughout.

Allbirds.blurb: The San Francisco footwear brand known for merino wool runners and loungers.
Allbirds.catalog_note: Only the all-wool pieces are listed; Allbirds' tree and sugarcane materials don't qualify.

Allwear.blurb: A basics brand making underwear, tees and loungewear in organic cotton.

Burt's Bees Baby.blurb: The baby and kids' line from the Burt's Bees family, known for GOTS-certified organic cotton pajamas, bodysuits and bedding.
Burt's Bees Baby.catalog_note: The pieces listed are 100% cotton. Pieces with elastane or incomplete fabric listings are left out.

Cottonique.blurb: A brand built for people with skin sensitivities, making underwear, socks and basics from 100% cotton with no latex or spandex.
Cottonique.catalog_note: The pieces listed are 100% cotton. Pieces with incomplete fabric listings are left out.

Coyuchi.blurb: A California organic-cotton brand, best known for bedding, with loungewear and robes.
Coyuchi.catalog_note: Most pieces are 100% organic cotton; a few add linen.

Elle & Riley.blurb: A cashmere label making sweaters, wraps and loungewear from Mongolian cashmere.

Fair Indigo.blurb: A Wisconsin brand making Fair Trade organic Pima cotton basics — tees, dresses and loungewear.
Fair Indigo.catalog_note: Nearly everything is 100% organic Pima cotton; a few pieces add elastane and are left out.

Filson.blurb: The Seattle outfitter founded in 1897, known for waxed cotton jackets, wool coats and heavy flannel shirts.
Filson.catalog_note: Filson also makes nylon and blended pieces; only the all-natural ones are listed here.

Harvest & Mill.blurb: A California brand making tees and basics from organic cotton grown and sewn in the USA, much of it undyed.
Harvest & Mill.catalog_note: The range is 100% organic cotton throughout.

Ibex.blurb: A merino wool outdoor brand making base layers, tees and jackets.
Ibex.catalog_note: Many Ibex pieces blend merino with nylon; only the all-wool items are listed.

Industry of All Nations.blurb: A Los Angeles brand making clothing with traditional methods and natural dyes — Peruvian cotton tees, alpaca knits, undyed basics.
Industry of All Nations.catalog_note: Nearly everything is a single natural fiber.

KENT.blurb: A brand making compostable organic cotton underwear with no synthetic elastic.
KENT.catalog_note: The range is 100% organic cotton by design.

Kowtow.blurb: A New Zealand brand making Fair Trade organic cotton clothing — tees, dresses, knits — with a stated circular-design focus.

Lake Pajamas.blurb: A Savannah, Georgia brand known for Pima cotton pajamas in signature stripes and prints, for the whole family.
Lake Pajamas.catalog_note: The range is 100% Pima cotton throughout.

Lezat.blurb: A small loungewear brand making leggings, tees and sets in organic cotton.
Lezat.catalog_note: Only the 100% cotton pieces are listed.

Linen Tales.blurb: A Lithuanian brand making clothing and home textiles from European linen.
Linen Tales.catalog_note: Most pieces are 100% linen; a few are natural blends. Pieces with elastane or incomplete fabric listings are left out.

Marle.blurb: A New Zealand womenswear brand making organic cotton, linen and wool pieces in muted colours.
Marle.catalog_note: Mostly 100% cotton; a few pieces are natural-fiber blends.

MATE the Label.blurb: A Los Angeles brand making organic cotton essentials — tees, sweats, dresses — dyed with low-impact dyes.
MATE the Label.catalog_note: Most of the range is 100% organic cotton; pieces with elastane are left out.

Mightly.blurb: A kids' brand making Fair Trade organic cotton clothing in bright colours.

Misha & Puff.blurb: A New England children's brand known for hand-knit sweaters and organic cotton basics with a heritage look.
Misha & Puff.catalog_note: Most pieces are 100% cotton or 100% wool.

Outerknown.blurb: A California brand co-founded by surfer Kelly Slater, making organic cotton tees, shirts and sweats.
Outerknown.catalog_note: Outerknown also uses recycled synthetics; only the all-natural pieces are listed.

PAKA.blurb: A brand making sweaters, socks and base layers from Peruvian alpaca.
PAKA.catalog_note: Mostly alpaca, with some cotton and a few natural-fiber blends.

Rawganique.blurb: A brand making clothing and footwear from organic cotton, hemp and linen, sewn in its own workshop with no synthetic components.
Rawganique.catalog_note: Cotton, hemp, wool and linen pieces, plus a few natural blends. Pieces with incomplete fabric listings are left out.

Ridge Merino.blurb: A Northern California merino wool brand making base layers and tees.
Ridge Merino.catalog_note: Mostly merino wool; pieces blended with synthetics are left out.

Ryker.blurb: A small menswear brand making wool and cotton basics.
Ryker.catalog_note: Wool and cotton pieces, plus a few natural-fiber blends.

Subset.blurb: An organic cotton underwear and basics brand, formerly Knickey.
Subset.catalog_note: Nearly everything is 100% organic cotton; pieces with elastane are left out.

Unbound Merino.blurb: A travel-clothing brand making merino wool tees, socks and layers meant to be worn for days without washing.
Unbound Merino.catalog_note: Mostly 100% merino. Pieces with synthetics or incomplete fabric listings are left out.

Wolk.blurb: An Antwerp brand making merino wool sleepwear and base layers.

Wool&Prince.blurb: A menswear brand known for merino wool button-down shirts and tees.
Wool&Prince.catalog_note: Mostly merino wool; a few pieces are linen or cotton.

WoolX.blurb: A New York merino wool brand making base layers, tees and socks.
WoolX.catalog_note: Only the all-wool items are listed; blends are left out.
